title: USMLE Step 1
description: First of three USMLE licensing exams. Pre-clinical sciences: anatomy, behavioral sciences, biochemistry, microbiology, pathology, pharmacology, physiology. As of January 2022 reported pass/fail (passing standard is approximately a 196 three-digit score).

questions.promptMd: A 25-year-old woman has weakness flexing her right elbow. The biceps brachii is innervated by which nerve?
questions.explanationMd: Musculocutaneous (C5-C7) supplies biceps brachii, brachialis, and coracobrachialis (the anterior compartment of the arm).

questions.promptMd: A patient cannot abduct their shoulder past 15°. The deltoid is innervated by:
questions.explanationMd: Axillary nerve supplies deltoid + teres minor; injury (e.g., humeral neck fracture) → loss of arm abduction beyond initial supraspinatus phase.

questions.promptMd: A patient develops weakness of foot dorsiflexion and eversion after fibular neck trauma. The injured nerve is:
questions.explanationMd: Common fibular nerve wraps the fibular neck; injury → foot drop (dorsiflexion + eversion loss).

questions.promptMd: The right coronary artery (RCA) supplies the SA node in approximately what percentage of patients?
questions.explanationMd: RCA supplies the SA node in ~60% of patients (right-dominant); circumflex covers SA in ~40%.

questions.promptMd: Damage to the recurrent laryngeal nerve during thyroidectomy most likely causes:
questions.explanationMd: RLN innervates intrinsic laryngeal muscles except cricothyroid. Unilateral injury → hoarseness; bilateral → respiratory distress.

questions.promptMd: The femoral triangle's contents from lateral to medial are:
questions.explanationMd: NAVEL: Nerve, Artery, Vein, Empty space, Lymphatics — lateral to medial. Used for safe femoral access.

questions.promptMd: A right-sided pulmonary embolus most commonly lodges in which area?
questions.explanationMd: PEs preferentially lodge in lower lobes due to greater blood flow; the right side has the more vertical, larger main bronchus and is statistically the most common site.

questions.promptMd: A lesion in the medial longitudinal fasciculus (MLF) produces:
questions.explanationMd: MLF connects CN VI (abducens) to contralateral CN III (oculomotor). Disruption → INO: affected eye fails to adduct on lateral gaze; common in MS.

questions.promptMd: Which structure does NOT pass through the diaphragm?
questions.explanationMd: Trachea bifurcates at T4 (well above the diaphragm). Mnemonic: 'I 8 10 EGGs At 12' — IVC at T8, esophagus at T10, aorta at T12.

questions.promptMd: A patient with a Pancoast tumor presenting with Horner syndrome has compression of which structure?
questions.explanationMd: Apical lung tumors compress the cervical sympathetic chain → ipsilateral ptosis, miosis, anhidrosis (Horner triad).

questions.promptMd: A 35-year-old man has had recurrent unwanted intrusive thoughts about contamination, and spends 4+ hours/day washing his hands. Most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanationMd: OCD: ego-dystonic obsessions + ritualistic compulsions performed to reduce anxiety. OCPD is ego-syntonic perfectionism without classical obsessions.

questions.promptMd: Which is consistent with major depressive disorder per DSM-5?

options.label: B
options.text: Depressed mood plus 4 additional symptoms for ≥2 weeks

options.label: C
options.text: Anhedonia plus 2 additional symptoms for ≥2 days

questions.explanationMd: DSM-5 MDD: ≥5 of 9 symptoms (incl. depressed mood OR anhedonia) for ≥2 weeks, with functional impairment.

questions.promptMd: A patient has a clear sensorium but cannot form new memories after a hippocampal lesion. The deficit is:
questions.explanationMd: Hippocampus is required for encoding new declarative memories. Damage → cannot form new memories (anterograde amnesia); old ones may be intact.

questions.promptMd: Confidentiality of patient information may be ethically broken when:

options.label: A
options.text: The patient asks the doctor not to tell anyone.

options.label: B
options.text: The patient threatens harm to a specific identifiable third party (Tarasoff).

questions.explanationMd: Tarasoff established a duty to warn or protect identifiable third parties when a patient makes a serious threat. Other exceptions: reportable diseases, abuse, gunshot wounds, court orders.

questions.promptMd: A 45-year-old patient with terminal cancer wants to refuse a life-saving blood transfusion on religious grounds. The patient is fully informed and demonstrates capacity. The physician should:

options.label: B
options.text: Respect the refusal — autonomy is paramount when capacity is intact.

questions.explanationMd: An adult with capacity has the right to refuse any treatment, even life-saving. Beneficence does not override autonomy.

questions.promptMd: A 22-year-old presents with disorganized speech, hallucinations, and delusions for the past 8 months, with significant social/occupational decline. Most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanationMd: Schizophrenia: ≥6 months of symptoms with ≥1 month of active psychotic symptoms + functional decline. Schizophreniform: 1-6 months. Brief: <1 month.

questions.promptMd: Which sleep stage shows EEG resembling waking but with skeletal muscle atonia?
questions.explanationMd: REM sleep features paradoxical EEG (low-amplitude, mixed-frequency like wake) with muscle atonia + dreams + erections.

questions.promptMd: A 6-year-old who used to be toilet-trained is now wetting the bed nightly after the birth of a sibling. This is best termed:
questions.explanationMd: Regression: reverting to earlier developmental behavior under stress.

questions.promptMd: Negative symptoms of schizophrenia include:
questions.explanationMd: Negative symptoms = absence of normal function: flat affect, poverty of speech (alogia), reduced motivation (avolition). Positive = hallucinations/delusions.

questions.promptMd: Korsakoff syndrome is associated with:

options.label: B
options.text: Thiamine (B1) deficiency, often from chronic alcoholism

questions.explanationMd: Thiamine deficiency → Wernicke (acute: confusion, ophthalmoplegia, ataxia) → Korsakoff (chronic: anterograde amnesia + confabulation). Damage to mammillary bodies.

questions.promptMd: Phenylketonuria (PKU) results from a deficiency in:
questions.explanationMd: PAH deficiency → phenylalanine accumulates → musty odor, intellectual disability if untreated; treated with low-Phe diet + tyrosine supplementation.

questions.promptMd: Cori disease (glycogen storage disease type III) is due to deficient:
questions.explanationMd: Cori (type III): debranching enzyme deficiency → limit dextrin accumulates. Hepatomegaly + hypoglycemia, milder than von Gierke.

questions.promptMd: Insulin signaling cascade involves which kinase activity?
questions.explanationMd: Insulin receptor is an RTK. Binding → autophosphorylation → IRS-1 phosphorylation → PI3K → Akt; ultimately GLUT4 insertion + glycogen synthesis.

questions.promptMd: An infant with seizures and lactic acidosis on a high-fat diet may have which deficiency?
questions.explanationMd: PDH deficiency → can't convert pyruvate → acetyl-CoA → lactate accumulates. Treatment: high-fat (ketogenic) diet bypasses PDH.

questions.promptMd: Northern blot detects:
questions.explanationMd: Mnemonic 'SNoW DRoP': Southern = DNA, Northern = RNA, Western = Protein.

questions.promptMd: A 9-month-old infant has hepatomegaly + hypoglycemia + 'doll-like face' + lactic acidosis. Most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanationMd: Von Gierke: severe fasting hypoglycemia + lactic acidosis + hyperuricemia + hyperlipidemia + hepatomegaly + doll face.

questions.promptMd: Hartnup disease causes:

options.label: B
options.text: Pellagra-like symptoms from impaired tryptophan transport (→ niacin deficiency)

questions.explanationMd: Hartnup: defect in neutral amino acid transporter → reduced tryptophan absorption → reduced niacin → pellagra-like symptoms (3 D's: dermatitis, diarrhea, dementia).

questions.promptMd: A patient with sickle cell disease has a single point mutation that converts:

options.label: A
options.text: Glutamate to valine at position 6 of β-globin

questions.explanationMd: HbS: missense Glu6→Val6 in β-globin. Hydrophobic Val promotes aggregation under deoxygenation → sickling.

questions.promptMd: Lesch-Nyhan syndrome results from deficiency of:
questions.explanationMd: Lesch-Nyhan: X-linked HGPRT deficiency → impaired purine salvage → hyperuricemia + neuro symptoms (self-mutilation, dystonia, intellectual disability).

questions.promptMd: Which describes the relationship between Km and substrate affinity?
questions.explanationMd: Km is the [S] at half-Vmax. Lower Km means the enzyme reaches half-Vmax at lower [S] — i.e., binds more tightly / higher affinity.

questions.promptMd: A Gram-positive cocci in clusters that is catalase positive and coagulase positive is most likely:
questions.explanationMd: Cluster + catalase+ → Staph; coagulase+ → S. aureus (vs. coagulase-negative S. epidermidis or saprophyticus).

questions.promptMd: Which organism is the leading cause of bacterial meningitis in young adults (16-21)?
questions.explanationMd: Meningococcus is the leading meningitis cause in college-age cohorts; outbreaks in dorms common. Pneumococcus more common in older adults.

questions.promptMd: A child has a 'pseudomembrane' in the throat after exposure to an unvaccinated traveler. Most likely organism?
questions.explanationMd: Diphtheria: gray pseudomembrane (fibrin + bacteria + dead cells) on throat. AB exotoxin inhibits eEF-2 (ADP-ribosylation).

questions.promptMd: TB skin test (PPD) cross-reactivity is a problem in patients with:
questions.explanationMd: BCG vaccine (M. bovis) → false-positive PPD. IGRA (interferon-gamma release assay) avoids the cross-reactivity.

questions.promptMd: A 30-year-old woman has dysuria and frequency. Urinalysis shows nitrites and leukocyte esterase positive. Most likely organism:
questions.explanationMd: Uncomplicated UTI: E. coli ~80%. Nitrites+ implies a Gram-negative urease-converting organism. Treatment: nitrofurantoin or TMP-SMX.

questions.promptMd: Which virus uses reverse transcriptase?
questions.explanationMd: Retroviruses (HIV, HTLV) use RT to convert their RNA genome to DNA for integration. Hepatitis B is unique in being a partially-dsDNA virus that also uses RT.

questions.promptMd: Which fungal organism is associated with bird and bat droppings in the Mississippi/Ohio River valleys?
questions.explanationMd: Histoplasmosis: Mississippi/Ohio River valleys, bird/bat droppings, intracellular yeast in macrophages. Cocci is SW desert; Blasto is Wisconsin/Great Lakes; Crypto is associated with pigeon guano (worldwide).

questions.promptMd: A patient with a productive cough + currant-jelly sputum + alcohol use disorder most likely has pneumonia from:
questions.explanationMd: Klebsiella pneumonia: classic in alcoholics + diabetics + aspirators; thick currant-jelly sputum due to mucoid capsule + RBCs.

questions.promptMd: Which antibiotic mechanism specifically targets the 50S ribosomal subunit?
questions.explanationMd: Macrolides (azithromycin, erythromycin), clindamycin, linezolid, chloramphenicol bind 50S. Aminoglycosides + tetracyclines bind 30S; quinolones target DNA gyrase.

questions.promptMd: An IV drug user develops tricuspid valve endocarditis. Most likely organism?
questions.explanationMd: S. aureus is the most common cause of acute IE in IV drug users; tricuspid is preferentially affected (right-sided injection inoculum).

questions.promptMd: Which represents the morphology of acute inflammation?

options.label: B
options.text: Neutrophilic infiltrate with edema and exudate

questions.explanationMd: Acute = neutrophils + vascular changes (vasodilation, edema, exudate). Chronic = lymphocytes/macrophages/plasma cells + scarring.

questions.promptMd: A 60-year-old smoker has hemoptysis. Chest CT shows a central lung mass with paraneoplastic SIADH. Most likely?
questions.explanationMd: Small cell lung cancer: central, smoking-strongly-associated, frequent paraneoplastic syndromes (SIADH, ACTH, Lambert-Eaton).

questions.promptMd: Which infarct type is characteristic of the brain?
questions.explanationMd: Brain undergoes liquefactive necrosis (high lipid + proteolytic enzymes). Most other tissues → coagulative.

questions.promptMd: An acute MI 4 hours after onset will show what gross/microscopic findings?

options.label: D
options.text: Dense scar with type I collagen

questions.explanationMd: Histologic changes are minimal in the first 4-12 hours. Coag necrosis + neutrophils appear at 12-24h. Macrophages 3-7d. Scar 2 months.

questions.promptMd: Diabetic nephropathy classically shows on biopsy:

options.label: C
options.text: Linear IgG deposits along the GBM

questions.explanationMd: Diabetic glomerulopathy: nodular mesangial expansion (Kimmelstiel-Wilson) + GBM thickening from non-enzymatic glycosylation.

questions.promptMd: Reed-Sternberg cells are pathognomonic for:
questions.explanationMd: RS cells (large cells with bilobed 'owl's eye' nuclei, CD15+/CD30+) are the histologic hallmark of Hodgkin lymphoma.

questions.promptMd: Apoptosis is characterized by:

options.label: A
options.text: Cell swelling + loss of membrane integrity + inflammation

options.label: B
options.text: Cell shrinkage + chromatin condensation + apoptotic bodies + no inflammation

questions.explanationMd: Apoptosis: programmed, energy-dependent, no inflammation. Cell shrinks; chromatin condenses; membrane stays intact; apoptotic bodies engulfed by neighbors.

questions.promptMd: BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations confer increased risk of:
questions.explanationMd: BRCA1/2 are tumor suppressors involved in DNA double-strand break repair. Mutations increase risk of breast (~70%), ovarian (~20-50%), prostate, pancreatic.

questions.promptMd: A patient with chronic hepatitis B is at increased risk for which neoplasm?
questions.explanationMd: Chronic HBV (and HCV) → cirrhosis + HCC. AFP is the classic tumor marker.

questions.promptMd: Crohn disease is characterized by:

options.label: A
options.text: Continuous mucosal inflammation limited to colon

options.label: B
options.text: Transmural skip lesions anywhere from mouth to anus + non-caseating granulomas

options.label: C
options.text: Crypt abscesses without granulomas + only colonic

questions.explanationMd: Crohn: transmural, skip lesions, granulomas, anywhere in GI tract. Ulcerative colitis: continuous, mucosal-only, colon, no granulomas.

questions.promptMd: A patient on warfarin has an INR of 8.0 with no active bleeding. Initial step?

options.label: B
options.text: Hold warfarin and give oral vitamin K

questions.explanationMd: INR > 5-9 without bleeding: hold warfarin ± low-dose oral vit K. Active bleeding: IV vit K + 4-factor PCC. Protamine reverses heparin, not warfarin.

questions.promptMd: Acetaminophen toxicity damages the liver via:

options.label: B
options.text: Saturation of glucuronidation/sulfation → CYP2E1 produces NAPQI → glutathione depletion

questions.explanationMd: Excess APAP saturates Phase II → CYP2E1 produces toxic NAPQI → depletes hepatic glutathione → centrilobular necrosis. N-acetylcysteine restores glutathione.

questions.promptMd: ACE inhibitors are contraindicated in pregnancy because:

options.label: B
options.text: They cause fetal renal damage / oligohydramnios / hypotension (especially 2nd-3rd trimester)

options.label: C
options.text: They are teratogenic in 1st trimester only

questions.explanationMd: Fetal renal blood flow depends on Ang II; ACE-I impair this → renal dysgenesis/dysfunction, oligohydramnios. All trimesters; especially 2/3.

questions.promptMd: Tricyclic antidepressant overdose is treated with:
questions.explanationMd: TCA toxicity → wide QRS + arrhythmia from sodium channel blockade. NaHCO3 alkalinizes serum + provides Na, displacing TCA from channels.

questions.promptMd: Which drug class treats benign prostatic hyperplasia by relaxing prostatic smooth muscle?
questions.explanationMd: α1-blockers (tamsulosin, doxazosin) relax prostatic + bladder neck smooth muscle → improved flow. 5α-reductase inhibitors shrink prostate over months.

questions.promptMd: Cisplatin's most common dose-limiting toxicity is:
questions.explanationMd: Cisplatin: classic dose-limiting nephrotoxicity (proximal tubular damage) + ototoxicity. Mitigated with hydration + amifostine.

questions.promptMd: Cytochrome P450 inducers (e.g., rifampin, phenytoin, carbamazepine) decrease plasma levels of:

options.label: A
options.text: Most coadministered drugs metabolized by CYP

options.label: B
options.text: Drugs eliminated unchanged by the kidney

questions.explanationMd: Inducers ramp up CYP enzymes → faster clearance → lower plasma levels of CYP-metabolized substrates. Prodrugs activated by CYP may have HIGHER levels of active metabolite.

questions.promptMd: Methotrexate inhibits:
questions.explanationMd: MTX competitively inhibits DHFR → less THF → impaired purine + thymidylate synthesis. Rescue: leucovorin (folinic acid).

questions.promptMd: A patient on lithium reports tremor + polyuria + worsening renal function. The mechanism most likely involves:

options.label: A
options.text: ADH receptor antagonism in collecting duct → nephrogenic diabetes insipidus

questions.explanationMd: Lithium → nephrogenic DI by impairing ADH (V2) signaling in collecting duct. Long-term: chronic interstitial nephritis.

questions.promptMd: Which beta-blocker is preferred for a hypertensive patient with comorbid asthma?
questions.explanationMd: β1-selective agents (metoprolol, atenolol, bisoprolol) avoid β2-mediated bronchospasm in asthmatics. Non-selective (propranolol) contraindicated.

questions.promptMd: Cardiac output equals:

options.label: B
options.text: Mean arterial pressure / total peripheral resistance

questions.explanationMd: CO = SV × HR is the kinematic definition; CO = MAP/TPR (rearranged from MAP = CO × TPR) is the hemodynamic version. Both true.

questions.promptMd: The Frank-Starling law states:

options.label: A
options.text: Stroke volume increases with contractility only

options.label: B
options.text: Stroke volume increases with end-diastolic volume (preload)

questions.explanationMd: Frank-Starling: greater preload → greater SV (within physiological range), via optimal sarcomere overlap.

questions.promptMd: In the loop of Henle, which segment is impermeable to water?
questions.explanationMd: Thick ascending limb is the diluting segment: H₂O impermeable, NaCl actively reabsorbed via NKCC2 (loop diuretic target).

questions.promptMd: Hypoxic vasoconstriction in the lung is unique because:

options.label: A
options.text: All vessels constrict in low O₂

options.label: B
options.text: Pulmonary vessels constrict in low O₂ to redirect blood to better-oxygenated alveoli

questions.explanationMd: Most vessels DILATE in hypoxia. Pulmonary uniquely constricts → matches perfusion to ventilation, reducing V/Q mismatch.

questions.promptMd: The respiratory chemoreceptor most responsive to acute changes in PaCO₂ is located:
questions.explanationMd: Central medullary receptors sense CSF [H+] (proxy for PaCO₂); they drive most of the minute-to-minute ventilatory response. Peripheral receptors respond to O₂ (mainly) + CO₂ + H+.

questions.promptMd: ADH increases water permeability in:

options.label: B
options.text: Cortical + medullary collecting duct (via aquaporin-2 insertion)

options.label: D
options.text: Loop of Henle as a whole

questions.explanationMd: ADH binds V2 → cAMP → AQP2 insertion → water reabsorption down the medullary gradient → concentrated urine.

questions.promptMd: A 2:1 second-degree AV block (Mobitz II) on ECG indicates:

options.label: B
options.text: His-Purkinje disease — risk of sudden complete heart block

questions.explanationMd: Mobitz II is INFRA-nodal (His-Purkinje) and unstable; can progress abruptly to complete heart block. Pacemaker indicated.

questions.promptMd: The stretch reflex involves:

options.label: B
options.text: One synapse (monosynaptic) between Ia afferent and α-motor neuron

questions.explanationMd: Patellar reflex: Ia afferent from muscle spindle → directly synapses on α-motor neuron → contraction. Reciprocal inhibition of antagonist via interneuron is also part of the response.

questions.promptMd: Aldosterone increases:
questions.explanationMd: Aldosterone acts on principal cells of the cortical collecting duct: ↑ENaC + ↑Na/K ATPase → Na reabsorption + K secretion. Acts on intercalated cells → H+ secretion.

questions.promptMd: Insulin's most rapid effect on cells is to:

options.label: B
options.text: Translocate pre-formed GLUT4 from intracellular vesicles to the plasma membrane

questions.explanationMd: Insulin's fastest effect (minutes): GLUT4 translocation in muscle + adipose. Transcriptional changes are slower.
